ukmt-jmo-2024-a01.prompt: What is the sum of the first nine primes?

ukmt-jmo-2024-a02.prompt: Forty-two cubes of side-length 1 cm are stuck together to form a solid cuboid. The perimeter of the base of the cuboid is 16 cm. What is its height, in cm?

ukmt-jmo-2024-a03.prompt: $PQRS$ is a square which has been divided into four regions: two identical rectangles, one square of area 9 cm$^2$ and a second square of area 25 cm$^2$. What is the area of square $PQRS$, in cm$^2$?

ukmt-jmo-2024-a04.prompt: Note that $49=4\times9+4+9$. How many two-digit numbers are equal to the product of their digits plus the sum of their digits?

ukmt-jmo-2024-a05.prompt: The difference between an interior angle of a regular polygon and an exterior angle of the same polygon is 150°. How many sides does the polygon have?

ukmt-jmo-2024-a06.prompt: When a group of five friends met up, Alice shook hands with one person; Bill shook hands with two people; Cara shook hands with three people; Dhriti shook hands with four people. How many people did Erin shake hands with?

ukmt-jmo-2024-a07.prompt: The time is 20:24 (expressed in 24-hour time). What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand on an accurate analogue clock, in degrees?

ukmt-jmo-2024-a08.prompt: We make a sequence of diagrams. The first diagram consists of a single node. The second diagram is made from the first diagram by drawing two edges of length 1 cm from that node, and putting a node at the other end of each new edge. After that, we make each new diagram from the previous diagram by adding two new edges to each node, with these new edges each having half the length of the edges that were added in the previous diagram. We also attach a node to the end of each new edge. The first four diagrams are shown. Find the total length of all the edges in the fifth diagram, in cm.

ukmt-jmo-2024-a09.prompt: The numbers $x$ and $y$ satisfy the equations $xy=\frac76$, $x(y+1)=\frac53$, $y(x+1)=\frac72$. What is the value of $(x+1)(y+1)$?

ukmt-jmo-2024-a10.prompt: What is the last digit of $2^{(2^{2024})}$?

ukmt-jmo-2024-b01.prompt: What is the smallest positive integer that only contains the digits 0 and 1, and is divisible by 36?

ukmt-jmo-2024-b02.prompt: Natasha and Rosie are running at constant speeds in opposite directions around a running track. Natasha takes 70 seconds to complete each lap of the track and meets Rosie every 42 seconds. How long does it take Rosie to complete each lap?

ukmt-jmo-2024-b03.prompt: The positive integers from 1 to $n$ ($n\ge2$) inclusive are to be spaced equally around the circumference of a circle so that: (a) no two even numbers are adjacent; (b) no two odd numbers are adjacent; (c) no two numbers differing by 1 are adjacent. What is the smallest value of $n$ for which the above is possible?

ukmt-jmo-2024-b04.prompt: My piggy bank contains $x$ pound coins and $y$ pennies and rattles nicely. If instead it contained $y$ pound coins and $x$ pennies, then I would only have half as much money. What is the smallest amount of money my piggy bank could contain, in pounds?

ukmt-jmo-2024-b05.prompt: A regular octagon $ABCDEFGH$ has sides of length 1. The lines $AC$ and $HF$ meet the line going through $D$ and $E$ at $P$ and $Q$ respectively. What is the length of the line $PQ$?

ukmt-jmo-2024-b06.prompt: Let $A$ be the set of $2n$ positive integers $1,2,3,\dots,2n$, where $n\ge1$. For which values of $n$ can this be split into $n$ pairs of integers in such a way that every pair has a sum which is a multiple of 3? As always in Olympiad problems such as this, you also need to explain why no other values of $n$ are possible.
ukmt-jmo-2024-b06.answer: All $n$ except those of the form $n=3k+2$ (i.e. possible exactly when $n\equiv0,1\pmod3$).
